issue: Ram drifted down slowly while release valve was closed; pump felt spongy during operation.
symptoms: Loss of holding pressure, spongy pump handle, visible oil seepage at hose fitting.
root_cause: Air trapped in hydraulic system after hose replacement; minor leak at tee coupler O-ring.
solution_applied: Bled hydraulic pump per manual procedure, replaced O-ring on tee coupler, refilled with hydraulic jack oil to correct level, pressure-tested to rated capacity.

issue: Pressure gauge reading unstable and bouncing during pressing cycles.
symptoms: Gauge needle fluctuates 500-1500 psi under steady load; occasional knocking sound from pump.
root_cause: Contaminated hydraulic oil and partially clogged gauge line.
solution_applied: Drained and flushed hydraulic system, replaced gauge hose, filled with fresh hydraulic jack oil, verified gauge calibration against known load.

issue: Hydraulic hose burst during bearing press operation near rated capacity.
symptoms: Sudden pressure drop, oil spray from hose near pump, operation stopped mid-cycle.
root_cause: Aged hose exceeded service life; operator exceeded recommended cycle pressure without monitoring gauge.
solution_applied: Replaced high-pressure hose and fittings, inspected all connections for cracks, retrained operator on maximum load limits and gauge monitoring.

issue: Release valve stuck; ram would not retract after pressing.
symptoms: Handle on release valve stiff, ram remained extended, pressure remained on gauge.
root_cause: Debris contamination in release valve seat from dirty work environment.
solution_applied: Disassembled and cleaned release valve, replaced worn seat washer, tested ram raise/lower cycle ten times under no load.

issue: Bed frame misalignment causing uneven pressure on workpiece.
symptoms: Workpiece tilts during press, uneven wear on bed plates, creaking from frame.
root_cause: Loose anchor bolts and worn lifting bar bushings after repeated heavy use.
solution_applied: Re-torqued floor anchor bolts, replaced lifting bar bushings, realigned bed plates and verified level with spirit level.

issue: Pump requires excessive handle strokes to build pressure.
symptoms: Slow ram travel, handle resistance lower than normal, longer cycle times.
root_cause: Low hydraulic oil level and worn pump seals.
solution_applied: Topped up hydraulic oil, replaced pump seal kit, bled system, verified full pressure within normal stroke count.

issue: Intermittent hydraulic leak at cylinder base during high-load straightening job.
symptoms: Oil pooling on floor after 20-ton load cycles, slight drop in max pressure.
root_cause: Damaged cylinder rod seal from side load on workpiece.
solution_applied: Replaced cylinder rod seal, installed alignment guide for workpiece, load-tested to 80% rated capacity before return to service.

issue: Safety guard bracket cracked after impact from falling tool.
symptoms: Visible crack in guard mount, guard shifted out of position, operator reported near-miss.
root_cause: Guard struck during maintenance; bracket not inspected before returning press to service.
solution_applied: Replaced guard bracket with manufacturer part, reinstalled guard, documented pre-use visual inspection checklist update.

issue: Press would not hold load; ram dropped 5 mm over 30 seconds under 10-ton load.
symptoms: Gradual ram descent, pressure gauge bleed-down, no external leaks visible.
root_cause: Internal check valve wear in pump assembly.
solution_applied: Rebuilt pump check valve assembly, replaced internal seals, performed hold test at 50% and 100% rated load.

issue: Unusual noise and vibration from pump during return stroke.
symptoms: Grinding noise on release, handle vibration, slow retraction.
root_cause: Air ingress through loose filler cap and low oil level.
solution_applied: Tightened filler cap, bled air from system, filled oil to mark, verified quiet operation over 20 cycles.

issue: Pressure gauge reads zero despite normal ram movement.
symptoms: Gauge stuck at 0 psi, ram still moves, no visible gauge damage.
root_cause: Failed gauge bourdon tube from over-pressure spike during improper spring compression attempt.
solution_applied: Replaced pressure gauge, installed overload warning label, briefed team on prohibited spring compression tasks.

issue: Hydraulic oil overheating during repeated production pressing cycles.
symptoms: Oil too hot to touch after 30 cycles, slower press response, burnt smell.
root_cause: Continuous duty beyond recommended cycle rate with insufficient rest intervals.
solution_applied: Implemented 5-minute cool-down every 25 cycles, changed oil, added cycle counter log for operators.

issue: Ram fails to extend fully; stops 20 mm short of normal stroke.
symptoms: Incomplete stroke, pressure builds then stalls, no external leak.
root_cause: Foreign debris on bed plate pins preventing full descent alignment.
solution_applied: Cleaned and inspected bed plate pins, removed metal shard from prior job, lubricated guide surfaces, verified full stroke.

issue: Operator reported hands slipping on pump handle; reduced control during pressing.
symptoms: Handle surface worn smooth, difficulty modulating pressure, near overtravel on small part.
root_cause: Worn handle grip and inadequate gloves for oily conditions.
solution_applied: Replaced pump handle grip, enforced heavy-duty glove requirement, added non-slip mat at operator station.

issue: Repeated failure to build pressure after cold start on morning shift.
symptoms: First cycles weak until afternoon, thicker oil behavior in cold bay, slow response.
root_cause: Hydraulic oil viscosity too high for unheated workshop in winter.
solution_applied: Switched to lower-viscosity hydraulic jack oil rated for cold service, warmed bay above 10C before first use, updated maintenance SOP.
